components.title: Bounded local live-capture publisher
components.summary: Publishes one selected interval's captured submit, result lifecycle and same-source observations as a bounded private atomic JSON record with writer identity and source hash.

components.title: Root-selected observer and producer publication reader
components.summary: Reads only selected private files, binds a root-published receipt to interval identities and file digests, then checks the correlated producer result and fixture observation.

flows.title: Physical capture to bounded publication verification

steps.description: Require a canonical selected path under an owned private anchor and refuse a preexisting capture target.
Project captured interval identities, writer/source metadata, submit, prior observation, result rows and preserved replacement/latest observations into the IPC record.
Declare capture readiness only after the exact terminal child lifecycle and enough fresh product lifetimes are observed.
Read the selected receipt, require exact packet/run/interval/nonce/submit/producer identity and reject stale or future publication.
Read bounded observer and native files, verify their receipt hashes, then select exactly one correlated native result.
Require the trusted receipt to bind the complete interval and both content digests before accepting the evidence join.

facts.statement: The live capture requires an owned mode-0700 anchor, writes a maximum 1 MiB record through an exclusive mode-0600 temporary file, and publishes it by link or rename with directory synchronization.
The capture projection carries public artifact identity, action, submit, prior/controller state, correlated results and observations; it deliberately does not project a credential or pairing field.
The source oracle reads a separately published receipt and verifies hashes and correlation; it states that it cannot create the producer or join receipt itself.
The candidate source explicitly retains two-peer result/fence comparison as an open gap, alongside native adversarial intervals and full callback atomicity.

The presence of this publisher, reader and source tests does not establish that an independent second peer emitted a factory-service result or fence record in a real run; runtime delivery remains unknown until separately custodied peer records are verified.
The work status accompanying this chapter reports the new independent peer observer implementation as IN PROGRESS and provides no delivered runtime record or native acceptance claim.

open_questions: Will the in-progress peer observer land at an exact engine revision and produce separately custodied result and fence records from two actual clients?
Which bounded join will prove that each peer record came from its own synchronized service state rather than a copied producer record?
